name: Observational: no wormhole throat has ever been observed

source.located: No single source: the claim is uncited at create.py:119/:249 (checked: create.py:115-122 carries no citation). The literature state it summarises is located as: Takahashi & Asada 2013, ApJL 768 L16, arXiv:1303.1301 (SQLS null, Ellis-wormhole abundance bound); Yoo, Harada & Tsukamoto 2013, arXiv:1302.7170 (GRB femtolensing bound); the echo series the tree itself lists in negmass.py:16-21 (1612.00266, 1712.09966, 1803.08565, 2010.07663, 2309.01894, 2512.24730); LVK 'Tests of GR with GWTC-3' (arXiv:2112.06861 / PRD 112 084080, echo search null); Chakraborty & Chakraborty arXiv:2509.13715 (the review detect.py reads: 'wormholes can mimic black hole shadows').

published_statement: No published statement is quoted by the tree. As returned by web-search snippets (NOT READ): Takahashi & Asada 2013: 'There are no multiple images lensed by the above two exotic objects for ~50,000 distant quasars in the SQLS data'; bound 'n < 10^-4 h^3 Mpc^-3 for a range of the throat radius a = 10-10^4 pc'; negative-mass compact objects n < 10^-8 (10^-4) h^3 Mpc^-3 at |M| > 10^15 (10^12) Msun. Yoo et al. 2013: n < 2x10^-9 AU^-3 for throat a ~ 1 cm (femtolensing). LVK GWTC-3: 'no evidence for ... post-merger echoes'. The tree's own record (negmass.py:16-26, READ locally): Abedi-Dykaar-Afshordi 1612.00266 'tentative evidence, ~2.9 sigma', Westerweck et al. 1712.09966 'LOW SIGNIFICANCE of evidence', reply 1803.08565 disputing; 'NO CONFIRMED DETECTION. The original claim is CONTESTED and the dispute is live'.
published_hypotheses: H-ID: 'observed' means IDENTIFIED as a wormhole by a discriminating channel; the shadow channel does not discriminate (detect.py:29-31, restating arXiv:2509.13715: 'Wormholes can mimic black hole shadows'), so imaged compact objects (M87*, Sgr A*) and LVK remnants are observations of objects not identified either way
H-MODEL: each null bound is for a specific metric family (Ellis / negative-mass point lens) and a lens model; a different b(r), Phi(r) moves it (detect.py:139-141 says the same of its own numbers)

H-WINDOW: each bound covers a throat-size window only -- SQLS a = 10..1e4 pc; femtolensing a ~ 1 cm; galactic microlensing SENSITIVITY quoted for a = 100..1e7 km (whether a BOUND exists there was not read)
H-STAT: the SQLS bound assumes a uniform comoving number density and the survey's selection function (snippet; assumptions not read at source)

H-CONTESTED: the GW echo channel carries one tentative positive claim (~2.9 sigma, 1612.00266) disputed by reanalyses and not supported by LVK O3 searches; 'no confirmed detection' is the consensus status, not 'no claim'
H-DATE: the statement is a status as of a date (2026-09 here) and moves with every new catalogue
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H-ID at create.py:119 ('NOBODY HAS EVER OBSERVED ONE') and create.py:249 (ROUTE_COST): the flat 'observed' silently means 'identified'; the tree's own detect.py:29-31 / :164 records that the shadow channel cannot discriminate, so the correct wording is 'no object has been IDENTIFIED as a wormhole' -- a wormhole could already be among observed compact objects (Astrobites 2026-04-11 snippet: supermassive objects 'might be wormholes in disguise'). This is a narrowing of the premise's wording, not a refutation.

DROPPED H-CONTESTED at create.py:119/:249 and in the rests_on sites (LEDGER.md:47/133 D24; specthm.py:1666-1669 W-enlarge note 'nobody has ever observed a throat'): the tree's own negmass.py:16-26 and index3.py:912 record a CONTESTED tentative echo claim; create.py states the absence flat. Note (against over-representation in either direction): echoes are an exotic-compact-object signature generically, and Abedi et al. did not claim a wormhole; the consensus 'no confirmed detection' agrees with create.py.

DROPPED H-WINDOW / H-MODEL in the rests_on use 'premise unpriced' (LEDGER.md:47 D24; specthm.py:1669 W-enlarge; index3.py:1048 'NOBODY IN THIS PROJECT HAS EVER ESTIMATED ONE [number density]'): published null results DO price the premise partially -- upper bounds on abundance in specific model classes and size windows (1303.1301, 1302.7170). None of those windows covers the tree's own search target (detect.py:90/103, a 1193 km throat, 11.4 orders below the SQLS window; computed), so for the tree's target 'unpriced' is accurate for these two bounds; for Ellis throats of 10 pc-10 kpc it is not.
ADDED nothing; WEAKENED nothing: the tree never asserts wormholes do not exist, only that none has been observed -- it does not overreach from 'not observed' to 'absent'.

(A) By AST over the tree (no import, no write): create.py:119 and ROUTE_COST carry the flat claim with no citation at :115-122; detect.OBSERVED = False and the shadow channel is recorded as non-discriminating; negmass.CONFIRMED_DETECTION = False, CONTESTED = True, 6 echo analyses listed, one tentative positive claim on record -- so the tree agrees with itself on 'no confirmed detection' and disagrees with create.py's flat wording on 'contested' and 'identified'. (B) Conditional on snippet values (NOT READ): SQLS bound gives Wigner-Seitz radius 13.37 Mpc/h and allows ~419 Ellis throats (10 pc-10 kpc) within 100 Mpc/h; the tree's 1193 km target (3.866e-11 pc) is 11.4 orders below the SQLS window and far from the 1 cm femtolensing point, but inside the quoted galactic-microlensing sensitivity window (100-1e7 km), for which no published bound was read. A negative observational claim itself has no derivation to re-run.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result: the claim is itself a statement ABOUT data, so the question is whether data now exist that the tree lacked. Evidence either way: (1) Against a moved conclusion: every channel the tree lists that has been run has returned null or contested -- SQLS lensing (null, bound), GRB femtolensing (null, bound), LVK O3 echoes (no evidence), with one tentative echo claim not confirmed; web-search snippets for 2025-2026 find only theoretical shadow/QNM work and no identification claim. So no datum located here moves 'no confirmed identification'. (2) For M's hypothesis in a narrower sense: the data that WOULD decide it are exactly what nobody has -- a discriminating channel (QNM spectrum, echoes, grey-body factors, negative-mass de-magnification) applied at the right size and model. The existing nulls cover model classes and windows that miss the tree's own 1193 km target (computed: 11.4 orders below SQLS), so for the tree's target the absence is an absence of search coverage as much as of objects. Having more data could change it; the data held do not. (3) The shadow data (EHT) are data the authors of a flat 'never observed' did have and did not discriminate with -- that is why the wording must read 'identified'. Not read at source this stage, so the literature half of this is corroboration from snippets plus the tree's own records, not a reading.
grade_evidence: The core (no confirmed identification of a wormhole, as of 2026-09) agrees with every record located: the tree's own detect.py (OBSERVED = False) and negmass.py (CONFIRMED_DETECTION = False), LVK GWTC-3 (no echo evidence, snippet), SQLS and femtolensing nulls (snippets). But the tree's use drops hypotheses its own files state, shown by AST in the rederive script: (i) 'observed' must be 'identified' -- detect.py records that shadows mimic, so imaged compact objects are observed and unidentified; (ii) the echo channel is CONTESTED (one ~2.9 sigma tentative claim, disputed), not a clean null -- negmass.py; (iii) 'premise unpriced' (D24, W-enlarge, index3.py:1048) overlooks published abundance upper bounds for Ellis throats (10 pc-10 kpc; ~1 cm), though computed here none reaches the tree's 1193 km target, where 'unpriced' remains accurate for those bounds. Not WRONG: nothing refutes 'no confirmed detection'. Not OPEN on the narrowing: the drift is shown from the tree's own READ records. CAVEAT, not flattened: the external sources were NAMED-NOT-READ this stage (alphaXiv quota exceeded, egress blocked); if the 'holds' half is required at source, that half is OPEN pending the reads below.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: create.py:119/:249 and the rests_on sites reworded to 'no object has been identified as a wormhole; the one tentative echo claim is contested; published nulls bound specific models and size windows, none at 1193 km' -- and the sources read at source (1303.1301, 1302.7170, 2112.06861, 2309.01894, 2512.24730, 2509.13715). To WRONG (for the flat wording): a confirmed identification -- a discriminating-channel detection (undamped/long ringdown, confirmed echoes, negative-mass de-magnification) accepted in the literature. To OPEN: if at-source reading is required and stays unavailable. To DATA-DEPENDENT: if the echo dispute were revived by a significant new analysis.
